newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH NFI 11 TO PUT BAND-AID MAKER ON BOURSE.
newsitem.headline: POLISH NFI 11 TO PUT BAND-AID MAKER ON BOURSE.

text.p: Poland's National Investment Fund (NFI) No. 11 plans a public offering late this year or early next for its Viscoplast SA adhesive bandage maker, and to put it on the Warsaw bourse early next year, a fund official said.
Fund capital markets director Jaroslaw Jasik told Reuters on Thursday that Viscoplast would issue 700,000 to 900,000 shares and be listed on the bourse's parallel floor.
"We plan an ex-rights issue for around the end of this year or early next and for the firm to be listed at the end of the first quarter or start of the second quarter next year," Jasik told Reuters.

He said the fund currently held 33 percent of Viscoplast's 1,056,000 shares, followed by the remaining 14 funds in the NFI mass privatisation programme, which have 27 percent, the state treasury with 25 percent, and employees with 15 percent.

Under the NFI scheme each of Poland's 28 million adults can buy one NFI unit and later exchange it for shares in each of the funds, which are run by domestic and foreign management firms and group more than 500 firms undergoing privatisation.
Viscoplast, one of Europe's largest adhesive bandage makers, expects to produce two million square metres of adhesive bandage this year.
Jasik said the issue's proceeds would go largely toward buying new equipment and upgrading distribution and marketing.
Jasik said the firm, based in the southwestern city of Wroclaw, made a net profit of 900,000 zlotys over this year's first half.
